commits.author: Jinhwan Suk (석진환)
commits.message:
[Refactor][RBLN] Dispatch block transfer on KVFormatSpec layout facts (#5667)

* [Refactor][RBLN] Dispatch block transfer on KVFormatSpec layout facts

RblnDeviceOps.multi_layer_block_kv_transfer gated its two op sequences on
exact EngineKVFormat values (NL_X_TWO_NB_NH_ONE_BS_HS / NL_X_NB_BS_HS).
Resolve the format to its KVFormatSpec once and dispatch on the layout
facts instead, matching the shared torch path after #4776:

- per-layer two-major HND (is_layer_list, is_hnd, is_two_major, not
  is_fused_packed) -> HND sequence
- per-layer [NB, BS, HS] MLA (is_layer_list, is_mla, not is_pbs_fused /
  is_kv_second_tuple) -> MLA sequence

The native 6-D layout and NL_X_TWO_NB_NH_BS_HS share those facts, so the
new kv_layout.hnd_layer_views squeezes 6-D tensors and passes 5-D ones
through. The spec registry is imported lazily because importing it at
module scope raises ImportError while lmcache resolves device_ops to
this module on an RBLN host.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>

* [RBLN] Drop speculative 5-D HND support from block transfer

vLLM-RBLN only allocates the 6-D NL_X_TWO_NB_NH_ONE_BS_HS layout, so
accepting 5-D NL_X_TWO_NB_NH_BS_HS tensors handled an input that never
reaches RBLN. Remove hnd_layer_views and go back to the strict
squeeze_singleton_axis: a 5-D cache passes the layout-fact check but
fails loudly in the squeeze.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>

* [RBLN][Test] Skip layouts RBLN refuses by design on the RBLN lane

RblnDeviceOps now moves only the layouts vLLM-RBLN allocates: per-layer
two-major HND (with the RBLN singleton axis) and per-layer [NB, BS, HS]
MLA. The MP tests that feed NHD, fused K/V, or 5-D HND caches therefore
fail on an RBLN host, by design rather than by regression.

Skip those 9 cases when torch_device_type is "rbln", under one
_UNSUPPORTED_ON_RBLN mark (plus the fused K/V round trip in
test_blocks_first_cs_kv_format). Every other device still runs them.

Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>

* [RBLN][Test] Drop RBLN skips from shared multiprocess and gpu_connector tests

The RBLN CI lane runs only tests/v1/platform/devices/rbln, so these
markers never take effect in CI, and RBLN refused these layouts before
this PR as well.

This reverts commit d0de6759.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>

* [RBLN] Refuse blocked-scale MLA pages; repack them in the torch fallback

NL_X_NB_BSV_BSS inherits is_mla from the per-layer MLA spec, so the RBLN
layout-fact dispatch admitted it and its whole-block copy wrote the
blocked [BS x vals][BS x scales] page into a chunk as if it were
token-major.

- KVFormatSpec: add the requires_blocked_scale_repacking layout fact,
  set only on NL_X_NB_BSV_BSS.
- RBLN: exclude that fact from the MLA predicate, so the format is
  refused with the layout ValueError.
- torch fallback: the MP block transfer splits each block into value
  and scale views and gathers/scatters token-major rows, matching the
  CUDA kernels.
- Tests: an RBLN refusal regression, a golden check that only
  NL_X_NB_BSV_BSS carries the fact, and a CPU round trip of the torch
  block transfer against a hand-written blocked page.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>

---------

Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Rui Zhang
commits.message:
[CI] Add CacheBlend coordinator global-match smoke to blend pipeline (#5747)

* [Coordinator][CacheBlend][Doc] Fleet blend lookup replaces the local matcher

blend_lookup.md described fleet CacheBlend matching as additive (local
matcher always runs, results unioned). The code skips the local matcher
whenever a coordinator client is configured and uses the coordinator's
matches as the only non-prefix source (lookup.py, unchanged since before
the #5012 refactor). Update the intro, lookup-flow diagram and steps,
rationale, gating note, failure-mode table, and code paths to match.

Signed-off-by: Rui Zhang <zrfishnoodles@gmail.com>

* [CI][CacheBlend][Coordinator] Add coordinator global-match smoke to the blend pipeline

Add a second step to .buildkite/k3_tests/blend/pipeline.yml that runs the
cacheblend-plugin's coordinator_match harness against the PR's LMCache: a
coordinator with --enable-blend-lookup plus two blend server + vLLM
stacks (gpt-oss-20b, --load-format dummy) sharing an fs_native L2. Stack B
must blend a body only stack A stored, found through the coordinator's
fleet blend index. Two GPUs, 40 min, one automatic retry.

run.sh now takes the test name as its first argument and dispatches to
scripts/run-<test>.sh; no argument keeps running the compat check.

Requires the plugin harness (.buildkite/harness/coordinator_match.py) on
CB_PLUGIN_REF.

Signed-off-by: Rui Zhang <zrfishnoodles@gmail.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: Rui Zhang <zrfishnoodles@gmail.com>

commits.author: Lin Sun
commits.message:
[Bugfix][ROCm][MP] Fix engine-driven fault on hipHostRegister'd memory (#5534)

[Bugfix][ROCm][MP] Use device addresses for registered host memory in block KV transfer

multi_layer_block_kv_transfer dereferences each LMCache object pointer
in the kernel. Engine-driven gather/scatter passes the host address of
slot views into the SHM pool, which EngineDrivenContextShm pins with
hipHostRegister. On ROCm the GPU maps registered host memory at a
different address (hipDeviceAttributeCanUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem
is 0 on MI300/MI355), so the kernel faults on the host address.

Only engine-driven transfer is affected. LMCache-driven transfer runs
the kernel on GPU staging buffers and moves data to and from host memory
with hipMemcpyAsync, which accepts registered host addresses.

On ROCm, resolve each object pointer with hipPointerGetAttributes and use
its devicePointer for host memory. CUDA builds are unchanged.

Signed-off-by: linsun12 <linsun12@amd.com>
Co-authored-by: Tony Lin <tony.lin@intel.com>

commits.author: Jinhwan Suk (석진환)
commits.message:
[Refactor][RBLN] Dispatch block transfer on KVFormatSpec layout facts (#5667)

* [Refactor][RBLN] Dispatch block transfer on KVFormatSpec layout facts

RblnDeviceOps.multi_layer_block_kv_transfer gated its two op sequences on
exact EngineKVFormat values (NL_X_TWO_NB_NH_ONE_BS_HS / NL_X_NB_BS_HS).
Resolve the format to its KVFormatSpec once and dispatch on the layout
facts instead, matching the shared torch path after #4776:

- per-layer two-major HND (is_layer_list, is_hnd, is_two_major, not
  is_fused_packed) -> HND sequence
- per-layer [NB, BS, HS] MLA (is_layer_list, is_mla, not is_pbs_fused /
  is_kv_second_tuple) -> MLA sequence

The native 6-D layout and NL_X_TWO_NB_NH_BS_HS share those facts, so the
new kv_layout.hnd_layer_views squeezes 6-D tensors and passes 5-D ones
through. The spec registry is imported lazily because importing it at
module scope raises ImportError while lmcache resolves device_ops to
this module on an RBLN host.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>

* [RBLN] Drop speculative 5-D HND support from block transfer

vLLM-RBLN only allocates the 6-D NL_X_TWO_NB_NH_ONE_BS_HS layout, so
accepting 5-D NL_X_TWO_NB_NH_BS_HS tensors handled an input that never
reaches RBLN. Remove hnd_layer_views and go back to the strict
squeeze_singleton_axis: a 5-D cache passes the layout-fact check but
fails loudly in the squeeze.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>

* [RBLN][Test] Skip layouts RBLN refuses by design on the RBLN lane

RblnDeviceOps now moves only the layouts vLLM-RBLN allocates: per-layer
two-major HND (with the RBLN singleton axis) and per-layer [NB, BS, HS]
MLA. The MP tests that feed NHD, fused K/V, or 5-D HND caches therefore
fail on an RBLN host, by design rather than by regression.

Skip those 9 cases when torch_device_type is "rbln", under one
_UNSUPPORTED_ON_RBLN mark (plus the fused K/V round trip in
test_blocks_first_cs_kv_format). Every other device still runs them.

Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>

* [RBLN][Test] Drop RBLN skips from shared multiprocess and gpu_connector tests

The RBLN CI lane runs only tests/v1/platform/devices/rbln, so these
markers never take effect in CI, and RBLN refused these layouts before
this PR as well.

This reverts commit d0de6759.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>

* [RBLN] Refuse blocked-scale MLA pages; repack them in the torch fallback

NL_X_NB_BSV_BSS inherits is_mla from the per-layer MLA spec, so the RBLN
layout-fact dispatch admitted it and its whole-block copy wrote the
blocked [BS x vals][BS x scales] page into a chunk as if it were
token-major.

- KVFormatSpec: add the requires_blocked_scale_repacking layout fact,
  set only on NL_X_NB_BSV_BSS.
- RBLN: exclude that fact from the MLA predicate, so the format is
  refused with the layout ValueError.
- torch fallback: the MP block transfer splits each block into value
  and scale views and gathers/scatters token-major rows, matching the
  CUDA kernels.
- Tests: an RBLN refusal regression, a golden check that only
  NL_X_NB_BSV_BSS carries the fact, and a CPU round trip of the torch
  block transfer against a hand-written blocked page.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>

---------

Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Rui Zhang
commits.message:
[CI] Add CacheBlend coordinator global-match smoke to blend pipeline (#5747)

* [Coordinator][CacheBlend][Doc] Fleet blend lookup replaces the local matcher

blend_lookup.md described fleet CacheBlend matching as additive (local
matcher always runs, results unioned). The code skips the local matcher
whenever a coordinator client is configured and uses the coordinator's
matches as the only non-prefix source (lookup.py, unchanged since before
the #5012 refactor). Update the intro, lookup-flow diagram and steps,
rationale, gating note, failure-mode table, and code paths to match.

Signed-off-by: Rui Zhang <zrfishnoodles@gmail.com>

* [CI][CacheBlend][Coordinator] Add coordinator global-match smoke to the blend pipeline

Add a second step to .buildkite/k3_tests/blend/pipeline.yml that runs the
cacheblend-plugin's coordinator_match harness against the PR's LMCache: a
coordinator with --enable-blend-lookup plus two blend server + vLLM
stacks (gpt-oss-20b, --load-format dummy) sharing an fs_native L2. Stack B
must blend a body only stack A stored, found through the coordinator's
fleet blend index. Two GPUs, 40 min, one automatic retry.

run.sh now takes the test name as its first argument and dispatches to
scripts/run-<test>.sh; no argument keeps running the compat check.

Requires the plugin harness (.buildkite/harness/coordinator_match.py) on
CB_PLUGIN_REF.

Signed-off-by: Rui Zhang <zrfishnoodles@gmail.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: Rui Zhang <zrfishnoodles@gmail.com>

commits.author: Lin Sun
commits.message:
[Bugfix][ROCm][MP] Fix engine-driven fault on hipHostRegister'd memory (#5534)

[Bugfix][ROCm][MP] Use device addresses for registered host memory in block KV transfer

multi_layer_block_kv_transfer dereferences each LMCache object pointer
in the kernel. Engine-driven gather/scatter passes the host address of
slot views into the SHM pool, which EngineDrivenContextShm pins with
hipHostRegister. On ROCm the GPU maps registered host memory at a
different address (hipDeviceAttributeCanUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem
is 0 on MI300/MI355), so the kernel faults on the host address.

Only engine-driven transfer is affected. LMCache-driven transfer runs
the kernel on GPU staging buffers and moves data to and from host memory
with hipMemcpyAsync, which accepts registered host addresses.

On ROCm, resolve each object pointer with hipPointerGetAttributes and use
its devicePointer for host memory. CUDA builds are unchanged.

Signed-off-by: linsun12 <linsun12@amd.com>
Co-authored-by: Tony Lin <tony.lin@intel.com>
